title: Candidate notebook — runtime architect quick notes
content:
Quick context:
- Candidate: senior systems engineer focusing on inference/runtime (resume shows distributed systems + 3 yrs model-serving)
- Interview format: 90m, split design + code + team fit
- My lens: shipping predictable latency at scale for LLMs; kernel/runtime tradeoffs; ops playbook

Top-line impression:
- Solid mental model for batching and headroom planning, pragmatic about fallbacks
- Gave concrete examples of reducing p50/p95 via prefix caching and early token pruning — liked the specificity
- Struggled slightly on how to measure regression in output quality after quantization (recommended A/B but fuzzy on metrics)

Strengths (short):
- Practical: lots of production anecdotes (cache invalidation snafu -> rollback script)
- Good at cross-team tradeoffs (SRE/infra/product)
- Knows kernel/FP16 vs int8 tradeoffs enough to propose experiments, including expected perf deltas

Concerns / red flags:
- Not yet run a large public-facing rollout with hard SLAs; most experience on smaller internal clusters
- Monitoring hygiene: relied on counts/alerts but less on automated eval sets / quality regression hooks (we need that as core)
- Tendency to default to conservative capacity buffers which could increase unit cost; would need nudges to think cost-first for hosted tenants

Deep dive notes (design):
- Autoscaling idea: candidate prefers workload-aware pods based on incoming token rate and observed KV cache hit ratio. Suggested heuristic: expand when pending request queue > threshold for 10s and median latency rising. Pros: simpler. Cons: brittle around spiky bursts.
- Cache invalidation: suggested TTL + versioned prefix keys. When I pushed on cross-model cache contamination, they proposed model-scoped cache namespaces (fine), but didn't propose a migration path for model pinning rollouts -> TODO: ask for rollout plan next round.

Coding / whiteboard (observations):
- Given a toy problem (simulate continuous batching loop), candidate produced pseudo-code quickly and identified race window on request grouping.
- Missed an edge case for partial responses and client disconnects; when prompted, described requeue semantics (good recovery thinking).
- Time management: nice pace, kept code readable but not micro-optimized — fine for screening stage.

Quality & eval thinking:
- Proposed offline evals + small production shadowing (10% traffic) before quantization. No concrete metric thresholds (e.g., BLEU / embedding drift) suggested.
- Mentioned using small prompt sets for regression alerts but did not explain selection method (bias risk).

Behavioral / team fit:
- Communicative, asks clarifying Qs early, pragmatic tradeoff framing (latency vs cost vs correctness).
- Comfortable owning incident postmortems; gave good example of blameless postmortem and action list.

Risk assessment & mitigations:
- Risk: cost-averse infra patterns (overprovisioning) -> Mitigate: pair with Optimize lead for batching/quantization experiments and add metric-based gating for scale decisions.
- Risk: insufficient evaluation coverage -> Mitigate: require a concrete eval plan before any quantized rollout (I wrote a skeleton in linked Confluence).

Suggested next steps:
- Interview loop: schedule a follow-up focused on operationalizing quantization + rollout plan with Product/Optimize folks (45m)
- Pairing: 60m pairing with an engineer to implement a simple cache eviction policy and a small load test script (verify race conditions they highlighted)
- Ask hiring committee: do we want someone who can immediately propose cost-saving experiments, or someone who stabilizes infra first? (I lean stabilizer with pragmatic cost wins)

Score (my quick):
- Technical (systems & runtime): 4/5
- Production-safety / SRE & incident ops: 4/5
- Eval & output-quality tooling: 3/5
- Collaboration / leadership: 4/5
- Overall (avg): 3.75/5 -> recommend move to pairing + quantization operational interview

Unresolved questions to ask next round (short list):
1) Give me a step-by-step rollout for int8 quantization for a 2B parameter model: can they name exact gates/metrics and rollback triggers?
2) How would they instrument quality regression at token-level for chat completions (what signals, what thresholds)?
3) If cache eviction is needed during a hot restart, how do they ensure correctness without request duplication?

Action items (me):
- Draft pairing exercise doc and attach to JIRA ENG-2147 (due 2025-11-18)
- Add candidate to Slack thread for scheduling (#hiring-runtime)
- Share this notebook with Marcus and Evan for quick reactions

Notes to self (raw):
- liked the postmortem details — suggests growth mindset
- follow-up emphasis should be on measurable evals and cost gating, not basic correctness
- keep an eye for candidates who default to overprovisioning; we need cost-first muscle for hosted product

End.
